routing.prompt: Critique the checkout screen: hierarchy, states, and copy.
Reshape the settings page UX; it's confusing to navigate.
Check the new onboarding flow in the running app before it ships, including accessibility.
Refactor this Vue component to the Composition API with script setup.
Write the release notes for version 3.2.

rules.task: You are asked to design a settings screen for a prototype. The prototype has no design system of its own. The design-system plugin is installed. There is no `~/design-system` folder.

options.plugin: take the look from the design-system plugin's design language
options.home-folder: look for `~/design-system/DESIGN.md` and take the look from it
options.fresh-identity: choose a palette, typeface, and layout concept for this prototype

rules.task: You are asked to design a settings screen for a prototype. The prototype has no design system of its own. The design-system plugin is not installed, and there is no `~/design-system` folder.

options.plain: design with no house style and tell the user once that the design-system plugin is missing
options.fresh-identity: choose a palette, typeface, and layout concept for this prototype
options.ask: stop and ask the user to install a design system first

rules.task: You are asked to design a settings screen in a repository that has its own design system in `docs/DESIGN.md` and `src/styles/tokens.css`. The design-system plugin is also installed.

options.repository: take the look from the repository's own design system
options.plugin: take the look from the design-system plugin's design language

rules.task: You simplified a dashboard screen in a running app that has Playwright installed, and are about to report the change. The user wants less text and fewer boxes on the screen.

options.count: run `ui-check.mjs --count` on the screen before and after the change and report the words, boxes, and controls
options.screenshots: describe the screen as simpler from before and after screenshots, without counts
options.budget: fail the change unless the screen has fewer than 200 words

rules.task: While simplifying a sign-up screen, you added the required consent sentence that the screen was missing. The word count rose by 14.

options.keep: keep the consent sentence and report the reason the count rose
options.cut: cut the consent sentence so the word count goes down
options.hide: move the consent sentence behind a closed disclosure so it is not counted

rules.task: You are asked to build the home page for a command-line tool that compares database schemas. The repository uses the design-system plugin's design language, and you have read its tokens and components.

options.sketch: sketch the page in the design system's tokens and components, check the sketch against what you would build for any developer tool, revise the parts that match it, and then build
options.direct: build the page with the design system's components, then review screenshots at 375px and desktop width, in light and dark, and refine
options.fresh-identity: choose a palette and typefaces that suit database tooling, and then build

rules.task: You are asked to redesign the existing settings page of an app, because users find it hard to navigate. The repository uses the design-system plugin's design language, and you have read its tokens and components.

options.sketch: sketch the new layout in the design system's tokens and components, check it against what you would build for any similar settings page, revise the parts that match it, and then rebuild
options.direct: rebuild the page with the design system's components, then review screenshots at 375px and desktop width, in light and dark, and refine

rules.task: You have sketched a new usage dashboard in the design system's tokens and components. The sketch puts a small all-caps label above each section heading and cuts every section into identical cards with the same radius and shadow. The design system does not prescribe either treatment.

options.revise: revise the section labels and the identical cards in the sketch, say what changed and why, and then build
options.build: build the sketch as planned, since the design system allows both treatments, and review screenshots afterwards

rules.task: You are asked to rename the Submit button on an existing settings screen to Save changes. The repository uses the design-system plugin's design language.

options.direct: change the label and check the screen
options.sketch: sketch the settings screen in the design system's tokens, check the sketch against the generic default, and revise the screen before changing the label

rules.task: You are building the product page for a command-line tool that compares database schemas. The design system sets the type, palette, and components, and leaves the first screen's content open.

options.subject: open with a real schema diff the tool produced, with the install command beside it
options.stats: open with a headline naming the tool, a large count of schemas compared with a small label, and three supporting stats

rules.task: You are building the public status page for a hosting service. Its readers come to learn whether the service is up right now. The design system sets the type, palette, and components, and leaves the first screen's content open.

options.stats: open with the current uptime as a large number with a small label, and supporting stats for the last 90 days
options.story: open with a headline about the team's commitment to reliability and a product image of the dashboard

rules.task: You are reviewing a documentation page that follows its design system. That design system's identity layer sets captions and metadata in its monospace face.

options.keep: treat the monospace captions as the design system's deliberate choice, not a finding
options.flag: report the monospace captions as a sign of a templated interface and ask for the body face

rules.task: You are reviewing a dashboard in a project that replaced its design system's identity layer with its own. The new identity names a sans-serif body face and a type scale, and says nothing about data labels. The dashboard sets its small data labels, such as stat captions and axis ticks, in a monospace face.

options.flag: report the monospace data labels as a sign of a templated interface and suggest the project's sans-serif face
options.keep: leave the monospace data labels, since nothing on the screen breaks
